name: Sett Rot / Pineapple Disease (Ceratocystis paradoxa)
conflict_resolution: Rainfall criterion removed (original text was qualitative: waterlogged sets). Temp/RH kept; overlaps cited optimum 21-22°C.
reference: ScienceDirect Topics: Ceratocystis paradoxa - most active ~21-22°C, inactive <10°C (not re-checked).
field_symptoms: Poor or uneven germination, rotting setts with characteristic pineapple-like fruity odour, blackening of internal vascular tissues, missing plants and weak shoots.
alert_logic: WATCH when wet-soil or drainage concerns occur during establishment. ELEVATED MONITORING when continuous soil moisture / rainfall coincides with sprouting. FIELD CONFIRMATION REQUIRED for affected setts or plants.
rule_conditions: Increase monitoring during establishment when planting setts are exposed to persistently wet, poorly drained, or waterlogged soil.
Optimal fungal growth occurs between 25–32°C with high relative humidity (85–100%) and leaf wetness >12 hrs.
Consider planting-material quality and field drainage.
Inspect cut sett ends for characteristic rotting and pineapple odour.
weather_parameters: Temp 20–26°C, RH 85–95%, VPD 0.12–0.50 kPa, Leaf Wetness 12–24 hrs

name: White Grub
conflict_resolution: No change. Partial support (soil temp ~25°C, monsoon rainfall, RH 68-75%).
field_symptoms: Root damage, yellowing, wilting, drying crowns, weak stunted growth, and presence of C-shaped white grubs in root zone soil.
alert_logic: WATCH in locally recognised endemic areas during monsoon showers (May–July). ELEVATED MONITORING when rainfall 20–80 mm/week and soil temp 25–32°C. FIELD CONFIRMATION REQUIRED when grubs or severed roots are found.
rule_conditions: In endemic areas, increase monitoring during locally reported seasonal activity periods following early rains.
Beetles emerge from soil after pre-monsoon showers and lay eggs in moist soil.
Inspect root zone soil around wilting stools.
Do not convert seasonal guidance into an unsupported rainfall threshold without scouting.
weather_parameters: Temp 25–30°C, RH 60–80%, VPD 0.63–1.70 kPa, Rain 100–200 mm, Leaf Wetness 4–8 hrs

name: Brown Rust
conflict_resolution: CORRECTED: temp 17-25 -> 17-27°C (optimum 17-27°C, onset needs min 17°C and 7 h wetness; declines at max >=32°C). Leaf wetness 7-13 h confirmed. RH/rain not numerically verified. Unsourced GDD removed.
field_symptoms: Elongated yellowish-brown flecks developing into reddish-brown to orange pustules on lower and upper leaf surfaces, leaf chlorosis and necrosis.
alert_logic: WATCH during moderate temperatures (20–30°C) with RH > 80% and prolonged leaf wetness (8–12 hrs). ELEVATED MONITORING in susceptible varieties (Co 86032, CoM 0265) and grand growth. FIELD CONFIRMATION REQUIRED on visible pustules.
rule_conditions: Monitor humid periods when foliage remains wet for extended periods (8–12 hrs minimum).
Western Maharashtra weather research confirms highest incidence when temperatures range between 20–30°C with high relative humidity (80–95%).
Recent rainfall and cloud cover together with leaf wetness are primary drivers.
Give greater attention to susceptible varieties and fields with rust history.
weather_parameters: Temp 17–27°C, RH 85–95%, VPD 0.10–0.53 kPa, Rain 50–150 mm, Leaf Wetness 7–13 hrs

name: Whiplash Smut
conflict_resolution: CONFLICT RESOLVED: temp 30-35 -> 25-30°C (germination optimum 25-30°C with peak at 30°C; smut incidence fell sharply at 35°C: 40.4% at 30°C vs 5.7% at 35°C). RH 65-75 -> >70%. Rainfall/leaf wetness kept, unverified.
reference: Bhuiyan et al. 2021, Phytopathology 111(11):1905-1918; Hidayah et al. 2024, J. Phytopathol. 172(2); Mol. Plant Pathol. 2025 review (PMC12712235)
field_symptoms: A long, black whip-like unbranched structure emerging from the apex / growing point; narrow upright leaves, thin spindly stalks and profuse tillering.
alert_logic: WATCH when warm dry periods alternate with rainfall (20–30°C, RH 75–95%). ELEVATED MONITORING in ratoon crops. FIELD CONFIRMATION REQUIRED immediately when whips emerge.
rule_conditions: Teliospores are wind-disseminated; infection occurs through nodal buds during tillering and early elongation.
Prioritise monitoring in fields with infected planting material or affected ratoon crops.
Inspect growing points and newly emerging leaves regularly.
weather_parameters: Temp 25–30°C, RH 70–100%, VPD 0.00–1.27 kPa, Rain 20–60 mm, Leaf Wetness 4–8 hrs

name: Pokkah Boeng
conflict_resolution: VPD corrected earlier (0.32-0.85). Temp 25-30 and RH 80-90 are consistent with field studies. "Shakoor et al. 2018" could not be found and is no longer cited.
reference: Ranjan et al. 2018, J. Pharmacogn. Phytochem. 7(5):2278-2280; ISSCT paper hosted at dochub.sasri.org.za (authors not confirmed)
field_symptoms: Wrinkling, twisting, shortening, chlorosis at base of young leaves; malformed growing points, top rot, ladder-like lesions inside stalk.
alert_logic: WATCH when warm moist weather (25–32°C, RH 80–95%, rain > 25mm) occurs. ELEVATED MONITORING when summer showers coincide with 3–7 month old crop. FIELD CONFIRMATION REQUIRED if twisted top leaves appear.
rule_conditions: Identify warm and moist weather periods.
Increase monitoring when warm, humid conditions coincide with summer showers, cloudy weather, or persistently wet conditions.
Give additional attention to plant crops approximately 3–7 months old and young ratoon crops.
Provisional temperature range 25–32°C with RH 80–95% represents high risk.
Do not issue confirmed disease alert from weather alone.
weather_parameters: Temp 25–30°C, RH 80–90%, VPD 0.32–0.85 kPa, Rain 150–300 mm, Leaf Wetness 8–12 hrs

name: Top Shoot Borer
conflict_resolution: CONFLICT RESOLVED: temp 26-32 -> 23-29°C (published optimum). Unsourced GDD 800-1500 replaced by published 718 degree-days above 14.1°C for the full life cycle. RH/rain/leaf wetness kept, unverified.
reference: Wei et al. 2021, J. Asia-Pac. Entomol. 24(3):814-818, doi:10.1016/j.aspen.2021.07.004
field_symptoms: Parallel shot holes in emerging leaf blades, red midrib tunneling, dead hearts in grown-up cane, and bunchy-top appearance due to side sprouting.
alert_logic: WATCH around monsoon onset / seasonal peaks (25–32°C, RH 70–95%, GDD 1000–3000). ELEVATED MONITORING during stem elongation. FIELD CONFIRMATION REQUIRED if shot holes or bunchy tops are observed.
rule_conditions: Seasonal pest with multi-generational broods correlated with monsoon showers and warm temperatures.
White moths lay egg masses covered with buff-coloured hairs on lower leaf surfaces.
Inspect spindle leaves for characteristic shot-hole punctures.
weather_parameters: Temp 23–29°C, RH 70–85%, VPD 0.42–1.20 kPa, Rain 80–200 mm, Leaf Wetness 5–9 hrs

name: Red Rot
conflict_resolution: No change. Optimum 25-31°C supported by Hisar field study (29.4-31°C) and Pusa weather study; revistacultivar/ResearchGate links not retrievable.
reference: epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IPPJ/article/view/22113; Dubey et al. 2020, J. Pharmacogn. Phytochem. 9(2)
field_symptoms: Yellowing and drying of 3rd and 4th leaves from top, longitudinally split cane showing dark-red internal tissue interrupted by white cross-bands and alcohol fermentation odor.
alert_logic: WATCH during wet monsoon periods (25–35°C, RH > 85%, rain > 30mm/week, GDD 2000–5000). ELEVATED MONITORING in waterlogged fields. FIELD CONFIRMATION REQUIRED on internal stem splitting.
rule_conditions: Weather data alone must not determine whether red rot is present.
Increase monitoring when wet conditions coincide with known disease history, susceptible varieties, or waterlogging.
Look for white cross-bands across reddened pith.
weather_parameters: Temp 25–30°C, RH 80–95%, VPD 0.16–0.85 kPa, Rain 100–250 mm, Leaf Wetness 8–14 hrs

name: Mealybug
conflict_resolution: Unsourced GDD 1200-1800 replaced by ~340 degree-days per generation above 17°C (quoted from Rae & De'ath by a later study - verify in original). Temp 25-32 consistent (max rate 30.4°C).
reference: Rae & De'ath 1991, Aust. J. Zool. 39(1):105-122, doi:10.1071/ZO9910105 (pink sugarcane mealybug, Saccharicoccus sacchari)
field_symptoms: Pinkish-white mealybug clusters attached beneath leaf sheaths around nodes, attended by ants, white powdery wax coating on rind.
alert_logic: WATCH during warm humid months (25–35°C, RH 70–90%). ELEVATED MONITORING under high plant density or drought stress. FIELD CONFIRMATION REQUIRED on nodal inspection.
rule_conditions: Colonises under tight leaf sheaths around nodes and root eyes.
High temperatures (25–35°C) and moderate-high humidity favor continuous breeding.
Pull back leaf sheaths on lower and middle nodes to scout colonies.
weather_parameters: Temp 25–32°C, RH 60–80%, VPD 0.63–1.90 kPa, Rain 40–100 mm, Leaf Wetness 3–6 hrs
